After compulsory prayers Allah was praised aloud; the poor are told to say Subhan Allah, Al-hamdu lillah and Allahu Akbar thirty-three times each; the Prophet's words of Allah's oneness.
Asked on the way from Mina to Arafat how Talbiya was said with the Prophet, Anas said people said Talbiya and Takbir, and neither was objected to.
Going up they said Allahu Akbar and going down Subhan Allah, told not to shout to One who hears and is near; returning, the Prophet said they return repentant, worshipping.
Instead of a servant from booty slave girls, the Prophet teaches Fatima and Ali bedtime words: Allahu Akbar 34 times, Al-hamdu lillah and Subhan Allah 33 each.
Ibn Abbas says Allah ordered His Prophet to glorify Him after all prayers, the meaning of 'after the prayers' in the verse.
Fatima asked for a servant for her mill-worn hands; the Prophet taught her and Ali to say Subhan Allah and Al-hamdu lillah thirty-three times and Allahu Akbar thirty-four at bedtime.
Coming from Khaibar, the camel carrying the Prophet and a wife slipped; Anas resaddled it, and nearing Medina the Prophet said they return repentant, worshipping and praising their Lord.
When the she-camel slipped and the Prophet and Safiya fell, Abu Talha covered her, and nearing Medina the Prophet kept saying they return repentant, worshipping and praising their Lord.
The poor were told glorifying, praising and magnifying Allah ten times each after every prayer would match the rich, and the Prophet declared Allah's oneness after each prayer.
Shouting Takbir is needless, for Allah hears and sees; 'La haula wala quwwata illa billah' is a treasure of Paradise; the Prophet praised Allah on heights and returning from journeys.
Declaring Allah's oneness a hundred times, or Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi, brings great reward; angels seek those remembering Allah, whom He forgives, and 'La haula' is a treasure of Paradise.
On a campaign the Prophet told those shouting Takbir they call the All-Listener, All-Seer, not the deaf or absent, and taught 'La haula wala quwata illa billah', a Paradise treasure.
Two phrases light on the tongue, heavy in the balance and beloved to the Gracious are 'Subhan Allahi wa bi-hamdihi' and 'Subhan Allahi-l-Adhim'.
Allah is as His slave thinks of Him and with him when he remembers Him, remembering him in return, and comes running to one who comes walking.
Two phrases dear to the Beneficent, light on the tongue and heavy in the balance, are Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi and Subhan Allah al-Azim.
